text:
erin: quick dump of the speculative decoding sweep i ran on draft-llama2-70b-quant this morning. wanted to capture raw numbers + a few notes before i forget. overall: ~2.1-2.4x throughput uplift depending on prompt mix, but a small hit on closed-book QA and some token-level hallucination patterns noted. looking for ideas on eval hygiene and whether to push this to dedicated canary.

ben: nice, thanks for the run. can you paste the exact config you used?

erin: pasted below. short summary first: batch=16, seq=1024, spec-k=4, accept-threshold=0.55, fallback-policy=best, quant=4bit-llm.q4_0. runtime used our optimized kernel set for nvlink boxes (p4d-like).

carla: fwiw the 0.55 threshold seems low — you get more fallbacks but better safety. what metrics did you track?

erin: perf: latency p50 down ~35%, p95 down ~28%, tokens/sec up 2.1-2.4x depending on prompt entropy. cost/unit token estimated -38%. quality: LAMBADA accuracy -0.9 pts, MMLU macro -0.3 pts (within noise), closed-book QA (NaturalQuestions top-1) -1.8 pts. hallucination heuristics (n-gram repetition/answer-shift) up ~0.6%.

dmitri: do you have per-prompt entropy bucket breakdown? speculative tends to blow up on low-entropy short prompts if acceptance threshold not tuned.

erin: yes — here's the script + config (run with ./spec_sweep.sh).

```bash
# speculative config snippet
MODEL=draft-llama2-70b-quant
BATCH=16
SEQ=1024
SPEC_K=4
ACCEPT_THRESH=0.55
FALLBACK_POLICY=best
QUANT=4bit-llm.q4_0
TOOLING_FLAGS="--use-kv-cache --enable-continuous-batching"
./run_inference --model $MODEL --batch $BATCH --seq $SEQ --spec-k $SPEC_K \
  --accept-thresh $ACCEPT_THRESH --fallback $FALLBACK_POLICY --quant $QUANT $TOOLING_FLAGS
```

erin: eval harness was the usual: 5 shards of heldout prompts (mix: 40% dialog, 30% long-form, 30% closed-book QA). temperatures 0.0 and 0.7 for deterministic/creative checks. sampling set to top-k=40 for nonzero temp runs.

eval-bot: automated eval report attached: 
- LAMBADA: baseline=72.1 -> speculative=71.2
- MMLU (macro): baseline=50.4 -> speculative=50.1
- NQ (top-1): baseline=49.0 -> speculative=47.2
- BLEU-style repetition metric: +0.6
- Throughput (tokens/sec): baseline=1200 -> speculative=2620

ben: thanks. that NQ drop is concerning for retrieval-backed products. any pattern in failure cases?

erin: manual inspection: failures cluster on questions requiring multi-step reasoning anchored in short context windows (<=40 tokens). hypothesis: speculative winners sometimes pick a plausible continuation that prunes search space away from the correct chain-of-thought, then fallback doesn't recover because accept threshold accepted early partial tokens.

carla: could you try two quick ablations: 1) lower spec-k to 2, keep threshold 0.55; 2) raise threshold to 0.7, keep k=4. want the delta numbers.

erin: running both now on the 1k sample shard. i'll post results when done.

erin: (update) ablation results:
- k=2, thresh=0.55: throughput +1.6x, NQ drop -0.9 pts, LAMBADA -0.4 pts
- k=4, thresh=0.7: throughput +1.9x, NQ drop -0.7 pts, LAMBADA -0.2 pts
so raising threshold looks better tradeoff; k=2 loses perf edge.

dmitri: interesting. implies many accepted spec outputs were borderline. raising thresh reduces false accepts. can you also capture the rejection rate distribution?

erin: rejection rate (fraction of requests that fell back) by bucket: low-entropy short prompts: 4.2%, mid-entropy dialog: 12.8%, long-form: 9.5%. with thresh=0.7 overall fallback drops to ~6.3% and perf still +1.9x.

eval-bot: regression alert heuristic: NQ drop >1.5 triggers here — current drop at 1.8 for default config. flagging for manual review.

erin: ok noted. for canary plan i propose: push thresh=0.7, k=4 to a small dedicated pool for 24h, route 5% traffic, enable per-request lineage and store speculative traces for failed QAs. also add a targeted prompt set for NQ-like items to the eval job so we can alarm faster. thoughts?

ben: +1 for conservative canary. also add a config to auto-fall back to non-speculative if NQ regression >1.0 on rolling window of 1h.

carla: agree. include a metric for "speculative-accepted-then-fallback-within-5-tokens" — that indicates wasted work and potential hallucination chains.

erin: good call. will add that metric and a small retention of speculative candidates (first 64 tokens) for offline analysis.

deploy-bot: canary job created: redwood-canary/speculative-thresh0.7-k4 -> 5% traffic, expires in 24h. (job id: canary-20260319-42)

dmitri: last note on eval methodology — make sure to include few-shot chain-of-thought style prompts in the QA shard. spec tends to be fragile there.

erin: will add a 200-example CoT subshard. thanks for the reviews everyone. i'll post a short doc with instructions on how to reproduce the sweep and the queries that failed NQ. :thumbsup:

ben: awesome. once we have canary telemetry we can decide whether this goes to dedicated stable.

carla: +1 — and log the random seed for runs (we saw variation before).

erin: seeds logged. saving artifacts to s3://redwood-eng/ml/spec-experiments/1791205432/

erin: end of thread.
